title: Description of a new species of Clypeoniscus Giard & Bonnier, 1895 (Isopoda: Epicaridea: Cabiropidae), a very large parasite of Aega psora (Linnaeus, 1758) (Isopoda: Cymothoida: Aegidae) from the fjords of Norway, with a review of epicarideans parasitizing cymothooid isopods
content:
Abstract
A new species of Clypeoniscus Giard & Bonnier, 1895 (Isopoda: Epicaridea: Cryptoniscoidea) is described based on a non-ovigerous female and a cryptoniscus larva from host isopods Aega psora (Linnaeus, 1758) collected in the fjords of Norway. This is the first species in the genus described from an aegid host. The new species is compared to all congeners as well as several undescribed cryptoniscus larvae reported from cymothooid hosts. Our molecular phylogenetic analysis using 18S DNA sequences from both specimens shows that they are conspecific and Clypeoniscus is correctly placed in Cabiropidae. Three putative species of cryptoniscus larvae recently reported from amphipod hosts belong to Cabiropidae and possibly Podasconidae, all of which are ectoparasitic on amphipods as adults. The criteria for counting coxal plate dentition is reviewed and clarified to exclude the ventromedial extensions of the coxal plates. Corrected coxal plate tooth counts for all taxa compared to the new species are provided. These findings, together with the reports of undescribed cryptoniscus larvae from diverse hosts, demonstrate that the diversity of cryptoniscoids remains substantially underestimated, even in some of the best-studied marine regions.
